title: The runbook: writing down what you did at three in the morning

videos.script: It is three in the morning, and an alert says the disk under the database is filling. {{alert}} You know this server. You also have one eye open, and the command you remember fixed a different problem last time. {{tired}} A runbook is the page you wrote in daylight for exactly this moment. One symptom. What to check, what to do about each thing you find, how to tell it worked, and whom to call when it did not. {{shape}} This lesson gives that page a fixed shape, so you can find the section you need in the dark. {{sections}} Then it writes one for a filling disk and runs every step on your server: df, du on the WAL directory, the replication slots, the log, and the largest tables. {{commands}} One step will surprise you. The fix works, and the directory does not get any smaller. The runbook has to say so, or the next person goes looking for a second problem. {{surprise}} While you work, you keep a log, one timestamped line at a time. {{log}} And at the end you read that log back, because a runbook nobody rehearses is only a guess. {{guess}}
